intro: Week 6 kicks off Sunday with Houston and Jacksonville at Wembley, and Baltimore goes to Cleveland without Lamar Jackson for a second straight week. Minnesota and Detroit rest on byes while San Francisco, Kansas City and Buffalo try to stay ahead, and Miami, Tennessee and the Chargers still look for a first win. 160 stories across all 32 teams.

top.label: Biggest Story
top.headline: Saints owner puts Kellen Moore and Mickey Loomis on notice at 1-4
top.dek: Gayle Benson warned her coach and general manager on Tuesday after New Orleans lost 23-13 to Minnesota. She said the staff must prepare the players and that she must hold the organization accountable. Moore said Wednesday that everyone has to get better.

top.label: Injury Watch
top.headline: Lamar Jackson misses a second straight game, Tyler Huntley starts at Cleveland
top.dek: Jackson is out with an ankle injury, along with center Cam Jurgens, defensive tackle Broderick Washington and tight end Matthew Hibner. Baltimore is 4-1, and Huntley has led the Ravens to three straight wins.

top.label: Player Spotlight
top.headline: Drake Maye threw for 374 yards and four scores at Las Vegas
top.dek: Maye went 26 of 34 with a 150.9 passer rating against the Raiders. He enters Sunday 102 passing yards shy of 8,000 for his career. Another 300-yard game would make him the first Patriots quarterback with back-to-back 300-yard games since Tom Brady in 2019.

top.label: Stat of the Day
top.headline: 239: Josh Allen's rushing yards lead every quarterback
top.dek: Allen ran for 121 yards against the Rams, the second most of his nine-year career. He also ties for the league lead with 21 completions of 20 or more yards.

top.label: What's Next
top.headline: Unbeaten Chiefs host the winless Chargers on Sunday
top.dek: Kansas City is 4-0 and Los Angeles is 0-5 for the 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff on CBS at Arrowhead. The Chiefs play without Rashee Rice and Josh Simmons, and the Chargers need a win before their bye.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.headline: Bills survive Rams in overtime thriller

stories.text: Allen finally wins an overtime game as Bills beat Rams 37-34
stories.summary: Buffalo went to SoFi Stadium on Monday night and left 4-1 after a 37-34 overtime win. Josh Allen had lost his first seven career overtime games, and he ran for 121 yards and a touchdown to end that streak. Greg Rousseau blocked a 48-yard Rams field goal in the extra period, then two long Allen scrambles set up the winning kick.

stories.text: Spencer Brown set to play, five Bills questionable at Las Vegas
stories.summary: Right tackle Spencer Brown went from limited Wednesday to full Thursday and will play Sunday, coach Joe Brady said. Receivers DJ Moore (shoulder) and Joshua Palmer (shoulder), lineman Ed Oliver (knee), lineman T.J. Sanders (shoulder) and cornerback Dee Alford (ankle) are all questionable. Moore, Oliver, Palmer and Alford sat out the Rams game, and Brady said any of them plays if he feels ready after pregame work.

stories.text: Josh Allen leads all quarterbacks with 239 rushing yards
stories.summary: Allen's 121 rushing yards against the Rams were the second most of his nine-year career. He leads every quarterback in rushing yards this season and is tied for the league lead with 21 completions of 20 or more yards. Buffalo ranks fifth in rushing offense at 158.0 yards per game.

stories.text: 32.8: Bills points per game, tied for first in the NFL
stories.summary: Buffalo scores 32.8 points a game, tied for the league best, and gains 396.2 yards a game, fourth in the NFL. The defense gives it back, though: 28.2 points allowed per game ranks 28th and 388.6 yards allowed ranks 30th. Buffalo also has nine giveaways in its last three games, four of them by Allen.

stories.text: Bills visit Raiders Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Buffalo (4-1) plays at Allegiant Stadium against a Raiders team that is 3-2. Las Vegas has 10 takeaways, tied for the most in the league, so ball security is the thing to watch after Buffalo's recent turnovers. Maxx Crosby has 36 pressures and will test the Bills' line.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.headline: Hafley sticks with Willis on the bye week

stories.text: Hafley says Malik Willis stays the starter at 0-5
stories.summary: Miami lost to Cincinnati to fall to 0-5, and coach Jeff Hafley shut down any talk of a quarterback change. Asked if Kyle McCord would start against the Jets, he said no and called Willis the team's quarterback. Hafley also said Willis needs to play better and that the staff will look at everything on the bye.

stories.text: Dolphins use the bye to sort a long injury list
stories.summary: Linebacker Jordyn Brooks (foot), right guard Jonah Savaiinaea (ankle), running back Jaylen Wright (foot), edge Robert Beal Jr. (hamstring), cornerback Reese Taylor (quad) and receiver Caleb Douglas (ankle) all sat out Tuesday. Cornerback JuJu Brents left the Bengals game with a stinger, and tight end Justin Joly is in the concussion protocol. Running back De'Von Achane is on injured reserve and is not expected back for the Jets game.

stories.text: Ollie Gordon II carries the backfield without Achane
stories.summary: With Achane out, the Dolphins ran for 217 yards against the Bengals, and Gordon carried much of that load. Miami's passing game gave back the gains: Malik Willis threw two interceptions and lost a fumble in the 31-24 loss. Fox Sports reported Achane suffered a torn ACL in Week 3 against Kansas City, which made Gordon the lead back.

stories.text: -62: Miami has the league's worst point differential
stories.summary: The Dolphins have scored 70 points, 14.0 a game, and sit 62 points in the red through five games. They scored a season-high 24 against Cincinnati and still have not held a lead at any point this season. Only Miami, Tennessee and the Chargers remain winless.

stories.text: Bye in Week 6, then the Jets on October 25
stories.summary: Miami is off this weekend and returns to face the New York Jets on October 25. The Jets play at New England on Sunday before that game. Hafley has not ruled out bigger changes to the roster and staff during the bye.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.headline: Patchwork line faces Jets pressure

stories.text: Patriots hit the Jets with a makeshift offensive line
stories.summary: New England has a backup at left tackle and a third-stringer at right guard heading into Sunday. The Jets blitz on 39 percent of snaps, fourth most in the league, and pressure on 40 percent, seventh most. The Patriots have won 14 of their last 15 meetings with the Jets at Gillette Stadium.

stories.text: A.J. Brown and Henderson questionable, Davis out
stories.summary: Cornerbacks Carlton Davis (neck) and Karon Prunty (hamstring) are out. Receiver A.J. Brown (ankle), running back TreVeyon Henderson (ankle), tackle Will Campbell (knee) and linebacker Christian Elliss (chest) are among the questionable. Patriots.com says cornerback Christian Gonzalez is expected to play.

stories.text: Drake Maye threw for 374 yards and four scores at Las Vegas
stories.summary: Maye went 26 of 34 with a 150.9 passer rating against the Raiders. He enters Sunday 102 passing yards shy of 8,000 for his career. Another 300-yard game would make him the first Patriots quarterback with back-to-back 300-yard games since Tom Brady in 2019.

stories.text: -5: the Patriots' turnover margin trails the Jets' +3
stories.summary: New England's minus-5 turnover differential ranks tied for 27th, while the Jets sit at plus-3, tied for sixth. The Patriots still hold the edge in yards, averaging 372.4 a game on offense (eighth) against 284.0 for New York (26th). Ball security decides this one.

stories.text: Jets visit Gillette Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: The Patriots (3-2) host the Jets (2-3) in an AFC East game. A win would put New England at 3-0 at home and 2-0 in the division. Watch how the rebuilt line handles the Jets' pass rush.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.headline: Jets defense is the early surprise

stories.text: Jets defense has turned a corner under Aaron Glenn
stories.summary: New York allows 19.2 points a game, fifth in the league and down from 29.6 last year, and has 17 sacks, tied for third. Rookie end David Bailey, the No. 2 pick, has five sacks, and the Jets already have six takeaways. The offense still ranks 27th in scoring at 18.6 points a game.

stories.text: Breece Hall and Adonai Mitchell out at New England
stories.summary: Running back Breece Hall (quad), receiver Adonai Mitchell (finger), guard Dylan Parham (knee) and edge Joseph Ossai (ankle) are out. Tight end Kenyon Sadiq (concussion), receiver Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle), linebacker Francisco Mauigoa (quad) and safety Dane Belton (knee) are questionable.

stories.text: Braelon Allen runs for 116 yards in place of Hall
stories.summary: Allen started for the injured Hall and carried 24 times for 116 yards and a touchdown in the 17-12 win over Cleveland. His 22-yard run gave New York the lead for good. With Hall out again, he is the lead back at New England.

stories.text: 8: sacks of Deshaun Watson in the Jets' win over Cleveland
stories.summary: The Jets sacked Watson eight times, three of them by rookie David Bailey, and held the Browns to 198 total yards. Cleveland led 12-10 until a mishandled punt snap gave New York the ball in scoring position. Garrett Wilson caught seven passes for 104 yards in the win.

stories.text: Jets at Patriots Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: New York (2-3) travels to Gillette Stadium for the first of two straight AFC East games. The Jets then face the winless Dolphins on October 25 after Miami's bye. Geno Smith has not thrown an interception but has been sacked 16 times, third most in the league.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.headline: Huntley steers Ravens at Cleveland again

stories.text: Lamar Jackson sits again, Tyler Huntley takes the Cleveland start
stories.summary: Jackson will miss a second straight game with an ankle injury, so Huntley starts his 13th game for Baltimore on Sunday. The Ravens are 4-1 and carry first place in the AFC North into Cleveland. Huntley has led them to three straight wins.

stories.text: Four Ravens out, three more questionable for Cleveland
stories.summary: Jackson, center Cam Jurgens, defensive tackle Broderick Washington and tight end Matthew Hibner are out. Guards Emery Jones Jr. and Andrew Vorhees and receiver Ja'Kobi Lane are questionable. Zay Flowers was limited in practice but carries no game designation.

stories.text: Huntley scores the winner in overtime at Atlanta
stories.summary: Huntley went 24 of 32 for 201 yards and two touchdowns in the Week 5 overtime win over the Falcons. He then finished the game with a one-yard touchdown run. He averages 6.4 yards per attempt this season, well below the 10.1 Jackson posted before his injury.

stories.text: 164.4: Rushing yards per game, third in the NFL
stories.summary: Baltimore runs for 164.4 yards a game, third best in the league, and Derrick Henry has 476 yards and seven rushing touchdowns. Cleveland has allowed only one rushing touchdown all season, so the ground game meets a real test.

stories.text: At Cleveland, Sunday 1:00 PM ET on FOX
stories.summary: The Ravens visit the Browns at Huntington Bank Field with first place in the division on the line. Watch Henry against a run defense that has been tough, and whether Huntley can find Flowers on crossing routes. Baltimore then hosts Cincinnati on Oct. 25.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.headline: Bengals hit the bye with Burrow back in form

stories.text: Bengals take the bye after a 31-24 win in Miami
stories.summary: Cincinnati beat the Dolphins to improve to 3-2 and heads into its open week. Joe Burrow said the team has to be better, pointing to dumb mistakes, and Zac Taylor cited two personal fouls and two red-zone fumbles. The Bengals face Baltimore after the break.

stories.text: Bye gives Chase, Higgins and Cook time to heal
stories.summary: Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and safety Bryan Cook have all missed time over the past two weeks. Chase was in the concussion protocol earlier this month and still caught six passes against Miami. The open week gives the group extra recovery time.

stories.text: Burrow throws four touchdowns to four receivers
stories.summary: Burrow went 23 of 32 for 190 yards and four touchdowns against Miami, with three of the scores coming in the first half. Chase caught one for his 58th career touchdown. Burrow also leads the NFL with five touchdown passes of 20 or more yards.

stories.text: 22: Straight field goals for Evan McPherson, a team record
stories.summary: McPherson made his 22nd consecutive field goal in Miami, passing Shayne Graham's old franchise mark of 21. Chase also moved past Isaac Curtis into third on the Bengals' career receiving yards list with 7,126.

stories.text: On bye, then Baltimore on Oct. 25 at 1:00 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Cincinnati is off this Sunday. The first game after the break is at Baltimore on Sunday, Oct. 25, at 1:00 PM ET on CBS. Taylor and Burrow have won 75 percent of their games after a bye since 2021.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.headline: Browns try to bounce back against first-place Ravens

stories.text: Browns look to fix the details after a loss to the Jets
stories.summary: Cleveland led by two late against New York, then a missed extra point, a long kick return and a high snap on a punt set up the winning score. Todd Monken said his team has not played a complete game this year. The Browns are 3-2 and host Baltimore.

stories.text: Judkins, Graham, Schwesinger all questionable vs. Ravens
stories.summary: Running back Quinshon Judkins, tackle Mason Graham, linebacker Carson Schwesinger and end Derek Barnett were limited Friday and are questionable. Quarterback Dillon Gabriel (back), tackles Kalia Davis and Mike Hall Jr. and guard Teven Jenkins are out. Jenkins will miss his sixth straight game.

stories.text: Andre Szmyt keeps kicking without a miss
stories.summary: Szmyt has made 24 straight field goals, the third-longest streak in Browns history. Cleveland has played tight games, so his leg matters, and the Ravens game looks like another close one.

stories.text: 50: Straight games without allowing a 300-yard passer
stories.summary: The Browns have gone 50 games without giving up a 300-yard passing day, the longest active streak in the NFL. Cleveland has also allowed just one rushing touchdown this season. The defense has been the steady piece.

stories.text: Home vs. Baltimore, Sunday 1:00 PM ET on FOX
stories.summary: Cleveland hosts the 4-1 Ravens at Huntington Bank Field with first place in the division at stake. Baltimore is without Lamar Jackson, so Tyler Huntley starts. Watch how the Browns handle Baltimore's third-ranked ground game and Derrick Henry.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.headline: Rodgers and Warren power Steelers to Tampa

stories.text: Rodgers keeps rolling as Steelers head to Tampa
stories.summary: Aaron Rodgers threw three touchdown passes for the third straight game in a 34-22 win over the Colts, a first for a Steelers quarterback since 2021. He opened 11 of 11. Pittsburgh is 3-2 and visits a 1-4 Tampa Bay team.

stories.text: Metcalf, Ramsey, Dean questionable; two receivers out
stories.summary: Receivers Roman Wilson and Ben Skowronek are out, and safety DeShon Elliott stays on injured reserve. DK Metcalf (illness), Jalen Ramsey (wrist), Jamel Dean (ankle), Rico Dowdle (toe) and Keeanu Benton (ankle) are questionable. Dowdle and Benton were full Friday.

stories.text: Jaylen Warren hits the big play twice against Indy
stories.summary: Warren ran 15 times for 101 yards, including a 50-yard touchdown, and caught six passes for 87 yards, including an 80-yard score. He became the first Steeler with a 50-yard rushing touchdown and an 80-yard catch in the same game. The NFL named him a Player of the Week.

stories.text: 4: Sacks in the last three games combined
stories.summary: The Steelers did not record a sack against Indianapolis until late in the fourth quarter. They have four total over their last three games. T.J. Watt leads the team with 4.5 sacks and faces an undrafted rookie quarterback Sunday.

stories.text: At Tampa Bay, Sunday 1:00 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Pittsburgh visits Raymond James Stadium. Baker Mayfield is out with a thumb injury, so rookie Jalon Daniels makes his third straight start. The Bucs rank second in rush defense, which puts the focus on Warren. The Steelers play the Saints in Paris next week.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.headline: Texans chase a second win at Wembley

stories.text: Texans end four-game skid with a 26-3 win in Nashville
stories.summary: Houston finally has a win after a rough opening month. The defense held Tennessee to 187 yards and forced two turnovers, and four Ka'imi Fairbairn field goals built a 12-3 halftime lead. C.J. Stroud ran in a 2-yard score in the third quarter to put it away.

stories.text: Montgomery, Pitre and Dell are out for London
stories.summary: Running back David Montgomery (groin), safety Jalen Pitre (shoulder) and receiver Tank Dell (knee) are all ruled out against Jacksonville. Linebacker Henry To'oTo'o (shoulder) and defensive back Ja'Marcus Ingram (elbow) are questionable after full practices Thursday and Friday. Pitre and Montgomery both got hurt in the win over the Titans.

stories.text: Will Anderson Jr. leads the NFL with 7.5 sacks
stories.summary: Anderson took down Cam Ward three times against Tennessee, all in the fourth quarter. He also leads the league with 10 tackles for loss. Only J.J. Watt and Clay Matthews had 7.5 sacks and 10 tackles for loss through five games since 1999, and now Anderson joins them.

stories.text: 5: straight 100-yard games for Nico Collins vs Jacksonville
stories.summary: Collins has topped 100 receiving yards in each of his last five meetings with the Jaguars. That is the longest active streak against a single opponent in the NFL. He needs 22 yards to pass Owen Daniels for third on the Texans' career receiving list.

stories.text: Texans meet the Jaguars at Wembley Sunday morning
stories.summary: Houston plays Jacksonville in London on Sunday, Oct. 18 at 9:30 a.m. ET on NFL Network. The Jaguars are 4-1 and lead the division by three games over the 1-4 Texans. Watch how Houston's pass rush handles a Jaguars line that lost left tackle Anton Harrison.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.headline: Colts look to reset against winless Titans

stories.text: Colts fall 34-22 at Pittsburgh as red zone drives stall
stories.summary: Indianapolis dropped to 2-3 after a loss to the Steelers. Only one trip inside the Pittsburgh 25 ended in a touchdown, and four drives stalled after first-and-goal. Jaylen Warren scored on an 80-yard catch and a 50-yard run, a double no player had managed since Herschel Walker in 1986.

stories.text: Dulin and Carlies out, Tyler Warren questionable
stories.summary: Receiver Ashton Dulin (hamstring) and linebacker Jaylon Carlies (ribs) are out against Tennessee. Tight ends Tyler Warren (groin) and Will Mallory (thumb) are questionable. Alec Pierce has not played since Week 2, which has thinned the receiver room.

stories.text: Jonathan Taylor has 398 yards and six touchdowns
stories.summary: Taylor ranks ninth in the NFL in rushing yards and tied for fourth in rushing touchdowns through five games. Pittsburgh bottled him up last Sunday, which sets up another heavy workload against a winless Tennessee team. He led the league with 18 rushing touchdowns last season.

stories.text: 4: kicks of 55 yards or longer for Spencer Shrader
stories.summary: Shrader made five field goals against Pittsburgh, including a 57-yarder and a 56-yarder. His four kicks of 55-plus yards with Indianapolis are the most in franchise history. The offense needed all of them because it settled for field goals in the red zone.

stories.text: Colts host the winless Titans on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET
stories.summary: Tennessee (0-5) visits Lucas Oil Stadium on Sunday, Oct. 18 at 1 p.m. ET on FOX. Indianapolis has won the last six meetings and leads the series 41-22. Daniel Jones has thrown for 1,021 yards with three touchdowns and four interceptions, so protecting the ball is the first thing to watch.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.headline: Jaguars lose Harrison before Texans in London

stories.text: Cam Little's 57-yarder beats Eagles 19-17 in London
stories.summary: Ameer Abdullah's 53-yard kickoff return left one second, and Little drilled the game-winner from 57 yards as time expired. Philadelphia had gone ahead 17-16 on a Jake Elliott field goal with eight seconds left. Jacksonville is 4-1.

stories.text: Left tackle Anton Harrison out after knee surgery
stories.summary: Harrison went on injured reserve and faces knee surgery. NBC Sports reports he could miss three to five weeks at minimum, and possibly the rest of the season. Cornerback Montaric Brown (hamstring) and long snapper Ross Matiscik (shoulder) are also out against Houston, and cornerback Jaylon Jones (hamstring) is questionable.

stories.text: Parker Washington torches Eagles for 124 yards, 2 TDs
stories.summary: Washington caught six passes for 124 yards and both of Trevor Lawrence's touchdown throws, including a 51-yarder in the first quarter. Lawrence finished 24 of 39 for 331 yards with one interception. Washington is a Pecan Grove, Texas native, so Houston is a homecoming opponent.

stories.text: 63.8: rushing yards allowed per game, best in the NFL
stories.summary: Jacksonville's run defense leads the league at 63.8 yards allowed per game. The pass defense ranks 30th at 266.2 yards per game. The Jaguars have eight takeaways and a plus-five turnover margin through five games.

stories.text: Jaguars host the Texans at Wembley on Sunday morning
stories.summary: Jacksonville faces Houston in London on Sunday, Oct. 18 at 9:30 a.m. ET on NFL Network. A win would give the Jaguars a four-game lead on the Texans after six weeks. Walker Little is expected to start at left tackle against a Houston pass rush led by Will Anderson Jr.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.headline: Winless Titans visit Indianapolis for answers

stories.text: Titans fall to 0-5 after 26-3 loss to Houston
stories.summary: Tennessee lost its fifth straight game and managed only a Joey Slye field goal. The Titans were outgained 329 to 187, took seven penalties for 83 yards and gave the ball away twice. Coach Robert Saleh said one game does not define the season, while Jeffery Simmons said the team is not playing winning football.

stories.text: Winston and Elliott out; Spears questionable at Indy
stories.summary: Safety Kevin Winston Jr. (shoulder) and defensive lineman Jordan Elliott (personal) are out. Running back Tyjae Spears (knee) did not practice Thursday and is questionable after a full session Friday. Cornerback Joshua Williams (pec) is also questionable but practiced fully all week.

stories.text: Cam Ward searches for a rhythm: 63.2%, 3 TD, 3 INT
stories.summary: Ward has 896 passing yards through five games. Against Houston he went 23 of 36 for 170 yards with an interception and took four sacks. Saleh remains confident in him, but Tennessee needs faster decisions and more throws downfield.

stories.text: 187: total yards for Tennessee, a season low
stories.summary: Houston held the Titans to 187 yards and a single field goal. Tony Pollard gained 52 yards on 14 carries, and Ward averaged 4.7 yards per attempt. The Texans held the ball for 34:39.

stories.text: Titans visit the Colts Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Tennessee plays at Lucas Oil Stadium on Sunday, Oct. 18. Indianapolis has won the last six meetings and leads the series 41-22. The Titans' defense has recorded multiple sacks in four straight games, so watch whether it can pressure Daniel Jones.

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.headline: Broncos win ugly, and Nix takes the heat

stories.text: Broncos survive Seattle in overtime, but the offense draws fire
stories.summary: Denver beat Seattle 17-14 in overtime on Thursday night to move to 4-2. Wil Lutz won it from 53 yards after Ja'Quan McMillian picked off Sam Darnold. The win came with loud criticism of Bo Nix and the late-game calls from the Prime Video booth.

stories.text: Surtain and Hufanga sat out, Moss was questionable
stories.summary: Cornerback Patrick Surtain II (ankle) and safety Talanoa Hufanga were out against Seattle, and cornerback Riley Moss was listed questionable with a rib injury. Denver held on without Surtain. The team has not said whether he returns for the Oct. 25 trip to Arizona.

stories.text: Ja'Quan McMillian ends it with an overtime pick
stories.summary: McMillian intercepted Darnold on Seattle's first possession of overtime, which handed Lutz the chance to kick the winner. The defense covered for an offense that managed 168 total yards.

stories.text: 168: total yards for a Denver offense that still won
stories.summary: The Broncos gained 168 yards against Seattle, and Bo Nix threw for 107 on 17-of-27 with no touchdowns. Two touchdown drives, 79 and 44 yards, produced the points. The other nine drives added two first downs and 45 yards.

stories.text: Denver gets a mini-bye, then heads to Arizona
stories.summary: The Broncos do not play this Sunday. Their next game is Oct. 25 at the Arizona Cardinals, kickoff at 2:05 p.m. The extra rest gives Surtain and Moss time to heal and Sean Payton time to fix the offense.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.headline: Unbeaten Chiefs host winless Chargers

stories.text: Unbeaten Chiefs come off the bye against 0-5 Chargers
stories.summary: Kansas City is 4-0 and fresh from its bye week as it hosts a Los Angeles team still looking for its first win. The Chiefs have a ground game that ranks near the top of the league and a quarterback playing well. Patrick Mahomes is 10-4 in his career against the Chargers.

stories.text: Rashee Rice and Josh Simmons are out vs. the Chargers
stories.summary: Wide receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring and knee) did not practice all week and is out. Left tackle Josh Simmons (back) is also out, and cornerback L'Jarius Sneed (knee) is questionable. Mahomes (knee) practiced fully and carries no designation. Andy Reid expects Rice back for Week 7.

stories.text: Kenneth Walker III leads the way on the ground
stories.summary: Walker has 537 rushing yards in four games, second in the NFL, and leads the league at 6.2 yards per carry. He averages 134.3 yards a game. He also leads the league with 39 forced missed tackles.

stories.text: 106.2: Mahomes' passer rating through four games
stories.summary: Mahomes has 1,037 passing yards, nine touchdowns and two interceptions, good for a 106.2 rating, fifth in the league. That kind of efficiency has the Chiefs fourth in the NFL in offensive EPA per play.

stories.text: Chargers visit Arrowhead on Sunday afternoon
stories.summary: Kansas City hosts Los Angeles on Sunday, Oct. 18 at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS at Arrowhead Stadium. Watch how the Chiefs handle the missing Rice and Simmons, and whether the run game stays hot against a Chargers defense that has been put on short fields.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.headline: Raiders try to stop a skid against Buffalo

stories.text: Raiders chase a third win in six games after a 3-0 start
stories.summary: Las Vegas opened 3-0 and has lost two straight. A loss to Buffalo on Sunday would drop the Raiders to 3-3. The defense forced nine takeaways in the first three games and just one in the last two.

stories.text: Three Raiders out, guard Zuhn questionable vs. Buffalo
stories.summary: Defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway (concussion), tight end Carter Runyon (foot) and wide receiver Dont'e Thornton Jr. (hamstring) are out. Guard Trey Zuhn III (knee) is questionable. Brock Bowers and Ashton Jeanty practiced and carry no game designation.

stories.text: Ashton Jeanty says he feels the best he has all year
stories.summary: Jeanty has 506 scrimmage yards, 215 of them as a receiver, and both of his touchdowns have come through the air. His ankle, a camp issue, came off the weekly practice report this week. He told reporters he feels the best he has all season.

stories.text: 9 to 1: Raiders takeaways, first three games vs. last two
stories.summary: Las Vegas led the league with nine takeaways through three weeks. In the two losses since, the defense has forced one. The Raiders will likely need to win the turnover battle to hang with Buffalo.

stories.text: Bills come to Allegiant on Sunday afternoon
stories.summary: Las Vegas hosts Buffalo (4-1) on Sunday, Oct. 18 at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS. Watch how the Raiders pressure Josh Allen and whether Bowers, who has 24 catches for 312 yards, finds room against a Bills pass defense.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.headline: Winless Chargers need a win at Arrowhead

stories.text: Chargers sit at 0-5 and look for answers in Kansas City
stories.summary: Los Angeles has yet to win and needs one before its bye week. Jim Harbaugh said he has spent most of his waking minutes figuring out how to win in Kansas City. The offense ranks last in EPA per play, and opponents have started 18 drives in Chargers territory, the most in the league.

stories.text: Alt, James and Harris are out against the Chiefs
stories.summary: Tackle Joe Alt (neck), safety Derwin James (hamstring), receiver Tre' Harris (hamstring), guard Kayode Awosika (fibula) and cornerback Donte Jackson (hamstring) are out. Six more players are questionable or doubtful. Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston are off the report and expected to play.

stories.text: Justin Herbert is running out of protection and patience
stories.summary: Herbert has five touchdowns and seven interceptions while completing 59.4 percent of his passes. Last week he went down five times behind an offensive line that has started multiple rookies because of injuries.

stories.text: 18: opponent drives starting in Chargers territory
stories.summary: That is the most in the NFL. New Orleans is second with 11. The Chargers defense ranks seventh in EPA per play, but short fields have made that number hard to see on the scoreboard.

stories.text: Chargers visit unbeaten Kansas City on Sunday
stories.summary: Los Angeles plays at Arrowhead Stadium on Sunday, Oct. 18 at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS. Watch the offensive line against the Chiefs' pass rush, and whether McConkey and Johnston can get open with Harris out.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.headline: Cowboys try to fix defense at Lambeau

stories.text: Cowboys bring in Pettine to repair a broken defense
stories.summary: Dallas lost 24-16 at home to a Tampa Bay team that had not won a game, and coach Brian Schottenheimer said the staff must be better. He added Mike Pettine as a senior assistant to coordinator Christian Parker. Pettine ran Green Bay's defense from 2018 to 2020, and the Cowboys face the Packers on Sunday night.

stories.text: Overshown a long shot, Lamb practices in full
stories.summary: Linebacker DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring) is questionable, and Schottenheimer called him a long shot. Corners Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) and Ameer Speed (knee) and tackle LT Overton (foot) are also questionable. CeeDee Lamb (thigh) went full all week after getting hurt against Tampa Bay.

stories.text: Pickens posts 130 yards in a loss
stories.summary: George Pickens caught nine passes for 130 yards and a touchdown against Tampa Bay. Lamb had 37 catches for 498 yards through four games, and Dak Prescott has thrown for more than 275 yards in four straight. The offense moves. The defense gives it back.

stories.text: 6.4: yards per play the Cowboys defense allows
stories.summary: That is the highest figure in the league. Dallas also ranks 31st in total defense and gives up 168.4 rushing yards a game, last in the NFL. Prescott is 1-5-1 in his career against Green Bay.

stories.text: At Green Bay, Sunday night on NBC
stories.summary: Dallas visits the 3-2 Packers on Sunday at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. Former Packers Kenny Clark and Rashan Gary play at Lambeau for the first time as visitors. Watch how Prescott handles a Green Bay defense that blitzes on 33.2 percent of snaps.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.headline: Tie with Washington keeps Giants on top

stories.text: Giants rally from 14 down to tie Washington in overtime
stories.summary: New York erased a 14-point deficit and finished 27-27 with the Commanders, then kept its hold on first place in the NFC East. The Giants outgained Washington 408 to 378. Dominic Zvada missed three of five field goals, all from 45 yards or longer.

stories.text: Thomas and Carter questionable, three ruled out
stories.summary: Cornerback Colton Hood (concussion), tight end Theo Johnson (neck) and safety Tyler Nubin (neck) are out against the Saints. Tackle Andrew Thomas (groin), tackle Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) and edge Abdul Carter (calf) are questionable. Quarterback Jaxson Dart remains out with a left knee injury.

stories.text: Winston throws three second-half touchdowns
stories.summary: Jameis Winston started 7 of 16 for 72 yards, then went 21 of 28 for 211 yards and three touchdowns after halftime. John Harbaugh said the tempo offense that sparked the rally should stick. Winston is starting because Dart is out for at least the rest of the regular season.

stories.text: 20: targets for Malik Nabers, a career high
stories.summary: Nabers caught 11 of them against Washington for his second straight 100-yard game. He has 27 targets over the last two weeks. Only six times in franchise history have the Giants had three straight 100-yard receiving games.

stories.text: Saints visit Sunday at 1 p.m. on FOX
stories.summary: New Orleans arrives at 1-4 for a 1 p.m. ET kickoff on FOX. The Giants have fumbled 10 times through five games, and the Saints have lost every game in which they finished minus in turnovers. Ball security decides this one.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.headline: Hurts out with blood clot, McKee starts

stories.text: Blood clot sidelines Jalen Hurts, McKee to start
stories.summary: Doctors found a superficial blood clot in Hurts' calf after the London trip. A follow-up ultrasound this week showed the clot moving, so the Eagles ruled him out for Carolina. The team has not said how many games he will miss, and CBS Sports says it could be more than one.

stories.text: Barkley, Hunt out; DeVonta Smith cleared
stories.summary: Saquon Barkley (hamstring), edge Jalyx Hunt (knee and ankle) and Michael Carter II (abdomen) are out, and Will Shipley went to injured reserve. A.J. Epenesa (back) is doubtful. DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks are cleared to play.

stories.text: Tanner McKee gets his first meaningful start
stories.summary: McKee has started twice, both in Week 18 games with the playoff picture settled. In the 2024 finale he threw for 269 yards and two touchdowns in a 20-13 win over the Giants. Now he leads a banged-up offense in a game that counts.

stories.text: 76: games at .500 or better, a streak that ended
stories.summary: The Week 5 loss to Jacksonville ended a franchise-record run of 76 straight games at .500 or better, per CBS Sports Research. Hurts has 933 yards, eight touchdowns and three interceptions through five games.

stories.text: Panthers at the Linc, Sunday at 1 p.m. on CBS
stories.summary: Carolina comes off a bye for the 1 p.m. ET game on CBS at Lincoln Financial Field. Without Barkley, Philly backs ran 16 times for 20 yards last week. Watch the run game and the line, where center Drew Kendall and guard Landon Dickerson are questionable.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.headline: Quinn on the hot seat before Monday night

stories.text: Clock blunder turns a win into a tie for Washington
stories.summary: In overtime against the Giants, Jayden Daniels scrambled for no gain with no timeouts left, and the clock ran out during a spike attempt before a field goal try. The 27-27 tie left Washington at 1-3-1. Dan Quinn, 18-20-1 in three seasons, admitted the late-game clock mistakes cannot happen.

stories.text: Mariota, McLaurin sit out Friday practice
stories.summary: Quarterback Marcus Mariota (knee), receiver Terry McLaurin (hamstring, rest) and running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) did not practice Friday. Stefon Diggs (hamstring) was limited. Daniels (left elbow) went full. Game designations were not posted on the report.

stories.text: Daniels runs for 103 in his return
stories.summary: Daniels returned from a two-game absence with a dislocated elbow and went 17 of 25 for 199 yards. He added two rushing touchdowns and 103 of Washington's 202 rushing yards. New York did not assign a spy to him.

stories.text: 202: rushing yards for Washington against New York
stories.summary: The Commanders ran for 202 yards and three touchdowns on the ground against the Giants. Daniels accounted for just over half the yards. It was not enough, since the Giants gained 408 net yards to Washington's 378.

stories.text: At the unbeaten 49ers, Monday at 8:15 p.m. on ESPN
stories.summary: Washington visits undefeated San Francisco on Monday, Oct. 19, at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. A Week 7 bye follows, then home games against the Eagles and Rams. Watch how Quinn's team handles the clock.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.headline: Williams nears return at Atlanta

stories.text: Bears try to bounce back from a 31-7 loss at Green Bay
stories.summary: Chicago fell 31-7 at Lambeau Field in Week 5 with Tyson Bagent starting. Bagent threw two interceptions before Case Keenum replaced him. The Bears now sit third in the NFC North and head to Atlanta on Sunday with their starting quarterback possibly back.

stories.text: Williams questionable, four Bears out vs. Falcons
stories.summary: Caleb Williams practiced fully for a third straight day and is listed questionable with a hamstring injury. He still has one more test to pass. Running back Kyle Monangai, linebackers T.J. Edwards and Keyshaun Elliott, and lineman Dayo Odeyingbo are out. Cornerbacks Kyler Gordon and Tyrique Stevenson are questionable.

stories.text: Caleb Williams, the Bears offense waits on his hamstring
stories.summary: Before he got hurt in Week 2 against the Vikings, Williams had completed 63.5 percent of his passes for 407 yards, 2 touchdowns and 1 interception. He added 65 rushing yards and 2 rushing touchdowns. He has missed the last three games.

stories.text: 4.4: Yards per carry the Bears defense allows
stories.summary: That number meets Bijan Robinson on Sunday. The Falcons back has 580 rushing yards on 102 carries, a 5.7 average, with 4 rushing touchdowns. Chicago's run defense ranks 24th in EPA per rush, and the unit allows the fourth-most yards per play in the league.

stories.text: At Atlanta, Sunday 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: The 3-2 Bears visit the 2-3 Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Watch whether Williams starts and how a thin front seven handles Robinson. Chicago hosts the Patriots on Thursday, Oct. 22.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.headline: Lions rest after a 45-21 rout

stories.text: Lions use the bye to chase the unbeaten Vikings
stories.summary: Detroit beat Arizona 45-21 on Oct. 11 to reach 3-2 and now trails 5-0 Minnesota by two games. The defense had allowed 31.8 points per game, 31st in the league, before that win. The Lions are off in Week 6 and host Green Bay on Oct. 25.

stories.text: White and Kennedy hurt in Arizona, bye buys time
stories.summary: Linebacker Devin White (forearm) and returner Tom Kennedy (knee) left the Cardinals game and did not return. Detroit has no game this week, so neither player has a designation to report yet. The team's own tracker, last updated Oct. 7, listed safety Brian Branch back at practice from a torn Achilles and safety Thomas Harper out until at least the Nov. 1 Green Bay game.

stories.text: Jared Goff throws three scores and runs one in
stories.summary: Goff went 19 of 30 for 279 yards and three touchdowns in Arizona, and he added a 1-yard rushing score. Jameson Williams caught touchdowns of 8 and 39 yards for his first multi-touchdown game as a receiver. Sam LaPorta added a 38-yard catch-and-run score.

stories.text: 58: Jahmyr Gibbs touchdowns before turning 25, a record
stories.summary: Gibbs ran for 151 yards and three touchdowns against the Cardinals. That pushed his career total to 58, past Barry Sanders at 57 for the most before age 25 in NFL history.

stories.text: Bye in Week 6, then Packers on Oct. 25
stories.summary: Detroit does not play this weekend. The Lions host Green Bay on Sunday, Oct. 25, at 4:25 p.m. Both teams are 3-2 right now, so the result will move the NFC North race.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.headline: Packers still waiting on Parsons

stories.text: Parsons will miss Week 6 as the medical staff holds him back
stories.summary: Micah Parsons is not practicing and will not play against Dallas. Matt LaFleur said he has had no setback but has not been cleared. Once he gets the green light, Parsons will need a week or two to get game-ready. The Packers have not ruled him out for Week 7 at Detroit.

stories.text: Four Packers out, five questionable vs. Dallas
stories.summary: Wide receiver Skyy Moore, cornerback Benjamin St-Juste and defensive tackles Jonathan Ford and Javon Hargrave are out. Defensive tackle Jordon Riley (Achilles) is doubtful. Guards Aaron Banks and Jacob Monk, defensive tackle Anthony Campbell, cornerback Brandon Cisse and receiver Savion Williams are questionable. Keisean Nixon and Lukas Van Ness carry no designation.

stories.text: Jordan Love carves up Chicago for 367 yards
stories.summary: Love went 25 of 31 for 367 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions in the 31-7 win over the Bears. Christian Watson caught six passes for 143 yards and scores of 42 and 53 yards. Matthew Golden added six catches for 123 yards.

stories.text: 24: Packers margin of victory over Chicago, their biggest since 2024
stories.summary: Green Bay's 31-7 win was its largest margin since a 34-0 win over the Saints in Week 16 of 2024. The defense forced five turnovers and held the Bears to 3.6 yards per play without Parsons. Edgerrin Cooper (Achilles) and Hargrave are the cost.

stories.text: Cowboys at Lambeau, Sunday 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC
stories.summary: The 3-2 Packers host the 2-3 Cowboys on Sunday Night Football. Dallas has alternated wins and losses all season. Green Bay then travels to Detroit in Week 7.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.headline: Unbeaten Vikings head into the bye

stories.text: Vikings reach 5-0 and the bye with a win over New Orleans
stories.summary: Minnesota beat the Saints 23-13 on Oct. 11 and enters its Week 6 bye. Kevin O'Connell called the timing a good chance to get healthy. Kyler Murray completed 24 of 30 passes for 229 yards and a touchdown, and he ran for 51 yards.

stories.text: Hockenson in concussion protocol, others due back
stories.summary: Tight end T.J. Hockenson left after two plays against the Saints and is in the concussion protocol, with a return expected for the Colts game. Jordan Addison (hamstring), Jordan Mason (thumb) and Christian Darrisaw (concussion) should return after the bye. Josh Oliver is out for the season, and guard Donovan Jackson needs surgery for a torn meniscus.

stories.text: Aaron Jones carries the load in Mason's absence
stories.summary: With Mason out, Jones ran 25 times for 113 yards and a touchdown against New Orleans. He now has 410 rushing yards this season. O'Connell praised his toughness. Cornerback Byron Murphy Jr. also picked off two passes.

stories.text: +6: Vikings turnover margin, best in the NFL
stories.summary: Minnesota leads the league in turnover margin at plus 6. The Vikings won the turnover battle 3-2 against the Saints, helped by two Murphy interceptions.

stories.text: Bye this week, then the Colts at noon on Oct. 25
stories.summary: Minnesota is off in Week 6. Its next game is against Indianapolis at noon on Sunday, Oct. 25, at U.S. Bank Stadium. Watch how many of the six injured regulars are back.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.headline: Penix set to start after rib scare

stories.text: Penix on track to start against Bears after rib injury
stories.summary: Michael Penix Jr. hurt his ribs late in regulation of Sunday's 30-23 overtime loss to Baltimore and had an MRI on Monday. Coach Kevin Stefanski says he feels better, and Penix practiced fully Friday with no game designation. Atlanta blew a 23-15 lead with 2:35 left and sits at 2-3.

stories.text: Henderson out, Za'Darius Smith questionable vs. Bears
stories.summary: Cornerback C.J. Henderson is out with a groin injury he suffered against the Ravens. Edge rusher Za'Darius Smith is questionable with a neck injury after clearing concussion protocol Thursday. Drake London (hip) and left tackle Jake Matthews (groin) were limited Friday. Rookie Avieon Terrell is in line for his first start if Henderson sits.

stories.text: Drake London keeps Atlanta's passing game moving
stories.summary: London caught seven passes for 118 yards against Baltimore and picked up four second-half first downs. Michael Penix Jr. also found Kyle Pitts Sr. for a 5-yard touchdown in the second quarter. London's hip is on the injury report, but he practiced Friday.

stories.text: 2.5: Za'Darius Smith leads the Falcons in sacks
stories.summary: Smith has 2.5 sacks, the most on the team, even though a neck injury kept him off nearly every snap the past two games. His status Sunday matters for a defense that gave up a late touchdown and a two-point try to force overtime against Baltimore.

stories.text: Bears visit Atlanta Sunday at 1 p.m. on FOX
stories.summary: The Falcons (2-3) host the Bears (3-2) at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, kickoff 1:00 p.m. ET on FOX. Watch Penix's rib after a hit, the pass rush if Smith plays, and who covers outside with Henderson out.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.headline: Eagles turn to McKee as Hurts sits

stories.text: Panthers get Tanner McKee after Hurts is ruled out
stories.summary: Philadelphia ruled Jalen Hurts out for Sunday with a blood clot, so Tanner McKee starts against Carolina. McKee has thrown 88 passes over the last two seasons. Panthers players said they learned the news Thursday and will prepare the same way regardless of who plays quarterback.

stories.text: Moton questionable, Freeling doubtful at Philadelphia
stories.summary: Running back AJ Dillon (ankle) is out and rookie tackle Monroe Freeling (knee) is doubtful. Taylor Moton (lung), Damien Lewis (elbow), Tershawn Wharton (neck), Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) and Trevor Etienne (ankle) are all questionable. Cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson remain on injured reserve.

stories.text: Bryce Young leads the league in passing yards
stories.summary: Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions in the 32-26 win over Detroit on Sunday Night Football. He completed 29 of 41 passes and leads the NFL in passing yards through four weeks. Chuba Hubbard added two rushing touchdowns.

stories.text: 88: passes Tanner McKee has thrown in two seasons
stories.summary: That is the sum of the Eagles quarterback's experience heading into Sunday, across six games and two starts. Carolina's defenders said they need to study his film because they know little about him.

stories.text: Carolina at Philadelphia Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS
stories.summary: The Panthers (2-2) visit the Eagles (2-3) at Lincoln Financial Field, 1:00 p.m. ET on CBS. Carolina comes off a bye. Watch the offensive line's health and how the secondary handles life without Horn and Jackson.

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.headline: Benson warns Moore and Loomis at 1-4

stories.text: Gayle Benson puts Moore and Loomis on notice
stories.summary: Saints owner Gayle Benson warned coach Kellen Moore and general manager Mickey Loomis on Tuesday after the team fell to 1-4 with a 23-13 loss to Minnesota. She said the coaches must prepare the players and that she must hold the organization accountable. Moore said Wednesday that everyone needs to improve.

stories.text: Elliss and Jennings out, Kamara and Olave questionable
stories.summary: Linebackers Kaden Elliss (calf) and Anfernee Jennings (knee) are out at the Giants. Running back Alvin Kamara (back), receiver Chris Olave (illness), tackle Nathan Shepherd (illness), cornerback Lorenzo Styles Jr. (knee) and long snapper Zach Wood (calf) are questionable. Quarterback Tyler Shough practiced fully Thursday with his left hand.

stories.text: Shough throws 48 times in Atlanta blowout
stories.summary: Tyler Shough completed 30 of 48 passes for 286 yards and one touchdown in the 45-24 loss to Atlanta in Week 4. After the Minnesota loss he took ownership of an interception and said penalties left the offense in long-yardage spots. He said his banged-up left hand did not affect him.

stories.text: 591: rushing yards the Saints have allowed
stories.summary: New Orleans has given up 591 rushing yards and nine rushing touchdowns through its first four opponents, at 5.1 yards per carry. Atlanta outgained them 205 to 50 on the ground in Week 4, with five of six touchdowns coming on runs.

stories.text: Saints at Giants Sunday, 1 p.m. on FOX
stories.summary: New Orleans (1-4) travels to MetLife Stadium to face the 3-1-1 Giants, 1:00 p.m. ET on FOX. Watch the run defense and whether Kamara and Olave are cleared to play.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.headline: Daniels starts again with Mayfield out

stories.text: Rookie Daniels starts again as Mayfield sits out
stories.summary: Baker Mayfield dislocated his right thumb in the Week 3 loss to Minnesota and is out for Pittsburgh. Coach Todd Bowles said Mayfield must be at full strength to play. Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels has 337 passing yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions through two starts and won his first against Dallas.

stories.text: Mayfield, Winfield out; Morrison doubtful vs. Steelers
stories.summary: Mayfield (right thumb), safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (rib) and receiver David Sills (hamstring) are out. Cornerback Benjamin Morrison (quad) is doubtful. Running back Sean Tucker, linebackers SirVocea Dennis and Josiah Trotter, and cornerback Ayden Garnes are questionable.

stories.text: Bucky Irving runs for a career-high 165 yards
stories.summary: Irving ran for 165 yards in the 24-16 Thursday night win over Dallas, the best game of his career. The Bucs also forced three takeaways, and Alex Anzalone sealed it with a late interception. It was Tampa Bay's first win of the season.

stories.text: 165: Irving's career-high rushing yards vs. Dallas
stories.summary: Irving's 165 yards powered the offense while Daniels attempted 25 passes and completed 19 for 189 yards and a touchdown. The ground game gives Tampa Bay its clearest path against Pittsburgh with a rookie quarterback.

stories.text: Steelers visit Tampa Sunday at 1 p.m. on CBS
stories.summary: The Bucs (1-4) host the Steelers (3-2) at Raymond James Stadium, 1:00 p.m. ET on CBS. Pittsburgh beat Indianapolis 34-22 last week behind three Aaron Rodgers touchdown passes. Watch how Tampa Bay replaces Winfield in the secondary.

teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.headline: Cardinals stick with Brissett amid skid

stories.text: Cardinals stay with Brissett through a four-game skid
stories.summary: Arizona has lost four straight, and each loss has come with the defense giving up 30 or more points. Coach Mike LaFleur is not changing quarterbacks. He says Jacoby Brissett was not the problem in the 45-21 home loss to Detroit, where Brissett threw for 292 yards and three touchdowns.

stories.text: Jeremiyah Love ruled out with lingering left ankle injury
stories.summary: LaFleur said Friday that the rookie running back will miss Sunday's game at the Rams, and nobody has discussed injured reserve. Love hurt the ankle in Week 4 against the Giants and did not practice Wednesday, Thursday or Friday. Safeties Wydett Williams Jr. (concussion) and Andrew Wingard (knee) are also out. Budda Baker, Kitan Crawford and Zaven Collins are questionable.

stories.text: Trey McBridge leads the Cardinals' receivers
stories.summary: McBridge caught nine passes for 66 yards and a touchdown against Detroit, the team high for the day. Brissett finished 29 of 47 in that game. Budda Baker added 11 tackles and a sack on defense.

stories.text: 32.4: points per game Arizona allows, most in the league
stories.summary: No defense in the league gives up more points than the Cardinals' unit. All four of their losses have included at least 30 points allowed. Paris Johnson Jr. is also done for the year with a torn biceps.

stories.text: Cardinals visit the Rams on Sunday
stories.summary: Arizona plays at SoFi Stadium on Sunday, Oct. 18, at 4:05 p.m. ET on FOX. LaFleur spent three years as McVay's offensive coordinator, so he knows the Rams' system well. Watch how the secondary handles Puka Nacua and Davante Adams, and how much Tyler Allgeier carries without Love.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.headline: Special teams sink Rams in overtime

stories.text: Rams fall to Bills 37-34 in overtime on special teams errors
stories.summary: Kyren Williams scored from a yard out with five seconds left to tie the game at 34. In overtime, Harrison Mevis had a 48-yard field goal blocked, and Buffalo's Tyler Bass then hit a 45-yarder to win. Mevis also missed from 50 yards in the first quarter, and Sean McVay said the kicking mistakes cost the game.

stories.text: McDuffie and Curl questionable for Cardinals game
stories.summary: Cornerback Trent McDuffie (groin) and safety Kam Curl (ankle) did not practice Friday and carry questionable tags. Tight end Davis Allen (foot) was limited Friday after sitting out the first two days. Wide receiver Alex Bachman, linebacker Nate Landman and cornerback Josh Wallace all practiced fully Friday.

stories.text: Puka Nacua catches 17 passes in the loss
stories.summary: Nacua set a career high with 17 catches on 24 targets for 138 yards and a touchdown. Matthew Stafford completed 40 of 54 passes for 383 yards and three scores. Nacua was the focus of the offense all night.

stories.text: 97: Davante Adams touchdowns inside the 20
stories.summary: Adams caught two touchdowns against Buffalo, from 4 and 5 yards out. The second pushed his career total of scores inside the 20 to 97. He also holds the all-time mark with 45 regular-season touchdowns inside the 5.

stories.text: Rams host the Cardinals on Sunday afternoon
stories.summary: Los Angeles plays Arizona at SoFi Stadium on Sunday, Oct. 18, at 4:05 p.m. ET on FOX. The Cardinals allow a league-high 32.4 points a game, so the offense should get chances. One report says Blake Grupe replaces Mevis at kicker after the Bills game.

teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.headline: Unbeaten 49ers host Commanders on Monday

stories.text: 49ers sit 5-0 and lead the NFC West heading into Monday night
stories.summary: San Francisco beat Seattle 32-29 in Week 5 to stay unbeaten. The defense produced four takeaways and five sacks in that win. The 49ers also host 94 former players this weekend for the 80th anniversary, and Keena Turner goes into the team Hall of Fame at halftime Monday.

stories.text: Bosa, Evans and Samuel miss Friday practice
stories.summary: Nick Bosa (knee, calf), Mike Evans (ribs, Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) all sat out Friday. Shanahan called the new Achilles issue for Evans soreness, and general manager John Lynch said there are no absolutes on Bosa's return. Defensive tackle Gracen Halton, defensive end Romello Height, safety Marques Sigle and linebacker Garret Wallow also did not practice.

stories.text: Brock Purdy has thrown 13 touchdowns through five games
stories.summary: Purdy is 98 of 142 for 1,196 yards and 13 touchdowns. He has thrown at least two touchdown passes and posted a 90-plus passer rating in every game. He is three touchdown passes shy of 100 for his career.

stories.text: 35.7%: the 49ers' pass pressure rate without Bosa
stories.summary: San Francisco is pressuring quarterbacks at about a league average rate this season, up from 29.1% last year after Bosa went down. The Seattle game hit 51.4%, their best since December 2023. Osa Odighizuwa has 15 pressures in five games.

stories.text: 49ers host Washington on Monday Night Football
stories.summary: San Francisco plays the Commanders at Levi's Stadium on Monday, Oct. 19, at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN and ABC. Washington is 1-3-1 and gets quarterback Jayden Daniels back from an elbow injury. A win would give the 49ers sole possession of the most Monday night wins in NFL history.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.headline: Seahawks stay with Darnold after OT loss

stories.text: Seahawks fall 17-14 in overtime at Denver on turnovers
stories.summary: Seattle trailed by 11 entering the fourth quarter, then scored a touchdown and a two-point conversion to force overtime. Sam Darnold's second interception in the extra period set up Wil Lutz's game-winning field goal. The Seahawks have lost three of their last four games, all by three points or fewer, and have turned the ball over 10 times in that span.

stories.text: Anthony Bradford nears a return at right guard
stories.summary: Mike Macdonald said Friday that Bradford has a good chance to be back for the Chiefs game. He has missed time since September with knee and hip injuries. Christian Haynes and rookie Beau Stephens have shared the right guard job in his absence. Linebacker Drake Thomas was out against Denver.

stories.text: Jaxon Smith-Njigba posts 12 catches for 134 yards
stories.summary: Smith-Njigba was cleared to play after an ankle injury the week before and led Seattle's passing game in Denver. Darnold went 27 of 51 for 278 yards with two interceptions and no touchdowns.

stories.text: 2: first downs Denver gained after its second-quarter touchdown
stories.summary: The Seattle defense shut the Broncos down for the final two and a half quarters and overtime. The offense could not cash in. Denver's Bo Nix finished 17 of 27 for only 107 yards.

stories.text: Seahawks host the Chiefs on Sunday Night Football
stories.summary: Seattle plays Kansas City at Lumen Field on Sunday, Oct. 25, at 8:20 p.m. ET (5:20 p.m. PT) on NBC. A loss would drop the Seahawks to 3-4. Macdonald has ruled out a quarterback change, so ball security is the thing to watch.
